title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is a case of synthetic media used to put words in a real person's mouth. The videos depicted a named political candidate making statements she did not make, and they were published to a social platform by a sitting officeholder's campaign. The failure is not that a model produced false content, but that the content was presented as authentic speech by a real individual and distributed as such.

The point of failure sits at publication, not generation. A generative tool can produce a fabricated clip of anyone, and nothing in the pipeline from prompt to post requires the depicted person to have said anything. Catching it would have required a check at the moment of posting, by the campaign or by the platform, that the depicted statements were actually made. No such check is described in the reporting.

What is not established is whether the videos violate defamation law, whether any legal action will follow the letter, and whether the campaign intended the clips to be taken as real. A cease-and-desist letter is an allegation, not a finding, and the campaign's public response does not settle the question.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including claims about corruption and free healthcare for undocumented immigrants. The letter, dated Sept. 30, points to a video shared Aug. 4 and says Cooke never made those statements.

Cooke's attorney argues the videos could violate state defamation law and says her team is monitoring Van Orden's accounts and weighing all legal options. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded with another AI video. Cooke lost to Van Orden by about 3 percentage points in 2024.
